claims.claim: The ECCV-submitted paper ("Beyond Realism: Directed Coverage for Correspondence Transfer", per Reviewer B's review title) claimed: (a) SDF-Fractal3D, an asset-free non-photorealistic procedural pipeline, transfers strongly zero-shot, so appearance realism is not the sole driver of transfer; (b) motion support is a primary driver; (c) 'directed coverage' (asymmetric overlap separating missing target support E->T from off-target mass T->E) feeds a compact ridge transferability estimator that ranks training sets without target training; (d) motion-only interventions (zoom/flip) on SDF-Fractal3D move transfer in the predicted direction.

ECCV headline estimator number: 'achieving up to 0.70 pairwise ranking accuracy under held-out evaluation targets, held-out training datasets, and joint held-out protocols'. Table tab:param_matched_results, row 'Flow (bidir.) + Appearance (bidir.), F×2 + A×2, k=4': Held-out T = 70.1%, Held-out B = 69.8%, Held-out (T,B) = 69.4%. Other rows: Flow bidirectional F×2 = 65.4%/65.6%/65.5%; Appearance MMD (symmetric) = 46.2%/44.3%/41.3% (below chance); Flow MMD (symmetric) = 58.7% in all three columns; Density-only (log n samples) = 52.4% in all three.

ECCV transfer grid (Table tab:tier0_representative_pair_grid_combined, mean PCK@5% averaged across CATs++ and RAFT): row 'SDF-Fractal3D' scored 68.9 (FlyingThings col), 89.0 (KITTI-2012), 90.5 (KITTI-2015), 46.6 (PointOdyssey); row 'FlyingThings' scored 80.6 / 96.2 / 93.4 / 55.0 on the same columns; row 'SDF-Fractal3D (Zoom)' is bold-best on KITTI-2015 (94.6), PF-WILLOW (32.0), TSS (46.3). So SDF-Fractal3D trailed real/established datasets on several benchmarks — the basis of Reviewer A's S-004 and Reviewer B's ceiling question.

Reviewer A (aL7M, alias S1/C4) recommended '1: Reject' at Confidence 4. Main objections verbatim: 'SDF-Fractal3D is introduced suddenly in the introduction, but how the authors design it is not written'; 'the dataset is built first, then its performance is observed, and finally, the metric is introduced to explain it'; 'The paper does not report the number of training samples used for SDF-Fractal3D'; 'the method remains an analysis tool rather than a practical method for dataset construction. Also, for the analysis tool, it's weak'; '0.70 pairwise ranking accuracy is not very useful'; 'Table 4 only shows small changes'; 'the results are averaged across model architectures, which obscures model-specific behaviors'.

Reviewer B (X9xv, alias S3/C2) recommended '3: Borderline Reject' at Confidence 2 and wrote 'I am open to improving my score if my concerns are properly addressed.' Main objections: 'How are extreme flow magnitudes (outliers) handled during the BFV normalization step?'; 'Is there a performance ceiling to the dataset? In Tab. 2, SDF-Fractal3D is quite behind some datasets on mean PCK'; long-tail flow magnitudes may 'heavily skew distance calculations in Euclidean space'; 'Would linear Ridge regression weights for pairwise flow generalize to architectures where temporal priors are the reason for transfer success (video foundation models, 4D tracking, etc)?'; 'Is treating dataset size as a nuisance parameter ... the correct approach?'; 'Does this mean that the estimator never to predict absolute performance?'; '2D warp variants achieve decent transfer because they're still seeing real paired images with valid displacement labels. How can we be sure of the claim that motion is primary?'; minor: HOF reduction, photorealism delta for SOTA, replace Supp Tab. 5-9 with heatmaps.

claims.claim: Reviewer C (mqfN, alias S2/C5) recommended '2: Weak Reject' at Confidence 5 (Expert). SDF-Fractal3D differs from other training sources in many ways besides photorealism'; motion interventions 'vary only a limited subset of motion factors and are conducted on a single synthetic family'; (2) 'the proposed directed coverage formulation feels somewhat heuristic and under-justified' (fixed-radius BFV vs cosine top-k HOF/DINO), estimator 'feels more like a careful feature-engineering pipeline than a principled new framework'; (3) 'A pairwise ranking accuracy of around 0.70 is above chance, but still far from reliable enough'; (4) averaging RAFT/CATs++ and mixing 'quite different training regimes' makes interpretation hard; wants 'controlled comparisons against synthetic pipelines that differ primarily in rendering realism while holding motion structure fixed'; (5) 'the baseline space is too narrow ... limited engagement with stronger modern transferability estimation ideas'; novelty 'somewhat incremental'.

claims.claim: ACCV draft explicitly tracks the ECCV review IDs: 'SDF-Fractal3D demoted from headline to instrument (addresses ECCV reviews P-001/P-002/S-004)'; 'P-007/P-013 ("0.70 not useful") answered by the ceiling section + Table 5; P-012/S-015/S-016 (causal overreach) by the pre-registered test + explicit Limitations; P-009 (absolute vs ranking) by Sec. 6 "anchors buy units, the rule buys order"; S-022 (baselines) by Table 2's symmetric/learned/appearance rows.'

ACCV draft scale answers the 'too limited' objections (S-019, S-006, S-020): '891 transfer evaluations (3 architectures in 9 training configurations × 11 synthetic training sets × 9 benchmarks; 99 trained models)'; architectures are CATs++, RAFT, and GLU-Net with pretrained/frozen 2×2 variants; all ranking is within (benchmark, architecture, variant) contexts (no architecture averaging); training sources are pure synthetic only (no mixed flow/semantic regimes in the grid).

claims.claim: ACCV reframes the '0.70 not useful' objection with decision metrics and a ceiling: the fit-free regime-aware policy 'ranks held-out sources, benchmarks, and both at rho≈0.5: parity with retraining a same-regime sibling variant, 73–76% of a three-architecture retraining consensus, and a median 1.2–2.8 PCK of top-1 selection regret versus 13.9 at random'; large-gap pairs ordered correctly '77–78%'. The internal finding doc gives the fit-free rule mean +0.498 vs inter-variant ceiling +0.528 (recovered fraction ≈0.99) and notes the fit-free metric 'beats every learned structure', converting Reviewer C's 'feature engineering' criticism into a supporting ablation ('the signal is in the measurement, not the model').

summary: The ECCV 2026 submission (paper 'Beyond Realism: Directed Coverage for Correspondence Transfer', sources in /home/spencer/Projects/ECCV_Reviews/eccv2026/) claimed that photorealism is not the sole driver of sim-to-real transfer for dense correspondence: SDF-Fractal3D, an asset-free non-photorealistic procedural pipeline, transfers strongly zero-shot across ~10 benchmarks; 'directed coverage' (asymmetric overlap separating missing target support E->T from off-target mass T->E in motion/appearance descriptor spaces) feeds a compact ridge estimator reaching 'up to 0.70 pairwise ranking accuracy' under three held-out protocols (best row F×2+A×2: 70.1/69.8/69.4%), and motion-only zoom/flip interventions move transfer as predicted (KITTI-2015 90.43 -> 94.94 with large-zoom, 84.72 with flip). Three reviewers, all negative: A (aL7M, Reject, conf 4) — unclear motivation, observation-driven narrative written as method-driven, missing SDF-Fractal3D sample counts, '0.70 pairwise ranking accuracy is not very useful', Table 4 changes small, architecture averaging obscures behavior; B (X9xv, Borderline Reject, conf 2, open to raising) — BFV outlier/long-tail normalization robustness, performance ceiling vs other datasets, ridge generalization to temporal/4D architectures, dataset-size-as-nuisance, absolute-vs-ranking, 2D-warp confound on the motion-primary claim; C (mqfN, Weak Reject, conf 5, expert) — causal claims exceed evidence (many confounds beyond realism; interventions limited to one synthetic family), directed coverage heuristic/under-justified, 0.70 only moderate, mixed regimes + averaging muddy interpretation, missing realism-only control, narrow baselines, incremental novelty. The current ACCV draft direction directly targets most of this: SDF-Fractal3D is demoted from headline to instrument (P-001/P-002/S-004); the headline becomes the regime-direction / two-cost law validated per-variant across 3 architectures × 9 variants × 11 pure synthetic sources × 9 benchmarks (891 evaluations, no averaging, no mixed regimes — S-006/S-019/S-020); '0.70 not useful' is answered by ceiling parity (rho≈0.5 ≈ inter-variant reproducibility ceiling, 73-76% of retraining consensus), selection regret (median 1.2-2.8 PCK vs 13.9 random), and gap-stratified accuracy (0.77-0.78 = cross-arch retraining at gaps >10 PCK) (P-007/P-013); causal overreach is met with a pre-registered out-of-sample grid test (off-target cost rho=+0.67, 8/9 flip p=0.029, appearance null p=0.43) plus an honest Limitations (P-012/S-015/S-016); absolute-vs-ranking gets its own section (P-009); the ridge-is-feature-engineering critique is inverted (fit-free policy beats every learned model — S-018); the HQ/matte texture-twin 2×2 supplies the missing realism-only control and recalibrates motion-primacy to specificity-not-magnitude (S-021/P-010, off-diagonal ties 91.1 vs 89.5); estimator unification (mean-NN + epsilon-coverage + KL contrast, HOF dropped) answers S-017/S-010/S-014. Still NOT addressed: BFV extreme-flow/outlier handling (S-007/S-008, no winsorization/clipping discussion found), SDF-Fractal3D training sample counts (S-003, not found), temporal/point-tracking architectures (S-013 — FlowFormer only pre-registered, results pending), modern transferability-estimator baselines (S-022 partial), and the pretrained half of the new law itself is observational-only — structurally the same gap Reviewer C punished. Notable internal red flag: the ECCV submission's Middlebury column came from a later-confirmed-buggy eval harness; ACCV excludes Middlebury entirely.
